earlier_scan.source_named: Anceaux, J.C. 1961. The Linguistic Situation in the Islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea — survey with phonological data on Marau; not reached online

sources.citation: Crossref API query 'Marau Yapen language' (20 rows); Wikipedia 'Marau language' and 'Yapen languages (Austronesian)'.
sources.note: No Marau-specific publication found; Wikipedia stub gives only 1,700 speakers (1987 SIL) and dialect Warabori.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record mara1397 (JSON + HTML page).
sources.note: Single reference (Anceaux 1961, Glottolog's most extensive description 'wordlist or less'); dialect Warabori (wara1296); no descriptive work listed.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily & Montreal Benesch. 2025. An un-Austronesian Austronesian language: Proto-Western Yapen and its lexicon. NUSA 77-78: 39-60. doi:10.15026/0002001226.
sources.note: Phonology content is limited to the reconstructed Proto-Western Yapen vowel and consonant inventories (five vowels plus *schwa; Table 1 consonants) and remarks that many wordlists fail to distinguish /β/ from /b/; the words 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' do not occur. Data: Usher's reconstructions plus Gasser's database of published and colleague-shared NW New Guinea wordlists. Cites Gasser, Arnold & Kamholz 2024 for modern Western Yapen phoneme inventories and Usher & Gasser (in prep.) 'A reconstruction of the Proto-Yapen lexicon'.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2017. Yapen contact (NUSA 62); Nuraeni & Hendrokumoro 2024 (Deskripsi Bahasa 6(2)); Sawaki, Yusuf. 2017. A grammar of Wooi (PhD ANU).
sources.note: Marau appears only as a neighbouring language (Sawaki: Marau-speaking villages Marau, Yenusi, Natabui); no Marau data or stress statement in any of the three.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily A. 2015. The development of verbal infixation in Cenderawasih Bay. In Malcolm D. Ross & I Wayan Arka (eds.), Papers from 12-ICAL, volume 3: Language change in Austronesian languages (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 018 / Studies on Austronesian Languages 004), 1-17. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. hdl:1885/13386.
sources.note: No statement about Marau stress or tone. The stress content is (a) Wamesa-specific: 'Stress in Wamesa is most often penultimate and falls on the infixed vowel on monosyllabic verb roots, such as [ˈri.a] 3sg-go, from the root /ra/. Stressed vowels are never reduced to glides.' (sect. 2, the text) and (b) general/reconstructive, footnote 11: 'It is plausible that PBY [Proto-Biak-Yapen] had largely penultimate stress and disyllabic roots, but this has not been definitively shown.. Stress throughout Austronesian is predominantly penultimate (Klamer 2002a; Blust 2009), but information on stress in…

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD diss., UC Berkeley.
sources.note: Marau data taken solely from Blust's ACD (source table); a few Marau cognates cited; no Marau phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Price, David S. & Mark Donohue. 2009. Report on the Ansus survey, West Yapen Island, Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-001.
sources.note: Phonological statement (App. IV) is for Ansus only (contrastive stress in Ansus); survey villages Ansus and Warabori, with Warabori and Natabui treated as Ansus-speaking; Marau only mentioned as a neighbouring, different language. No Marau data or stress statement.

sources.citation: Clouse, Helja (data) in Chan, Eugene (ed.). Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: 'Marau, Yapen, Papua, Indonesia'. Data dated 11 January 1993, 'taken from SIL linguistic survey list, 1992' (SIL Irian Jaya). MPI-EVA lingweb.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Numerals 1-10 only: ko-siiri, ko-iru, toru, a'ti, riŋ, wona, itu, wa'ru, si'u, haura. Three forms carry an apostrophe before the final syllable (a'ti, wa'ru, si'u), unexplained -- in SIL survey transcription this is usually a stress mark, but it could be a glottal stop; no prose statement. Wordlist-only data.

sources.citation: Capell, A. 1976. General picture of Austronesian languages, New Guinea area. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 5-52. Canberra: Australian National University. hdl:1885/253009.
sources.note: Nothing on Marau (or Yapen) prosody. Searched the whole ANU text with spaced-scanned-tolerant patterns for Marau, stress, accent, tone, tonal, pitch, penult, prosod, Yapen/Japen: the single Marau token is the trial pronoun ('Anceaux's lists (1961) give singular i < *iya and plural si, isi, ki < *siDa, with three that look like petrified trials: Papuma soru, Pom tioru, Marau hioru..', the text layersection on pronominal subgroups); the single 'stress' token is figurative ('The bulk of the stress in NG languages is laid on the person and number of actors', line 589); the 'tone' hits are all sub…

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Entry 178 MARAU: c. 1200 speakers, three dialects, 'Source: Anceaux 1961 (N, Wl, Cp)'; appendix comparative wordlist 178 Marau (~40 items from Anceaux) with no stress marks; no stress statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J.C. 1961. The linguistic situation in the islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea. Verhandelingen KITLV 35. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. 166 pp.
sources.note: Marau data = 'Own material: short word-list' (p. 3); section E p. 7 gives only villages, three dialects and c. 1200 speakers; the transcription note p. 14 says 'Stress-accent, vowel pitch and vowel length.. are not indicated'; the only accent remark in the book concerns Papuma (p. 7). Nothing on Marau stress.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen). Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Maraw', Provinsi Papua (idb 535). Online language-map record based on Badan Bahasa's dialectometric survey (Kampung Webi, Distrik Yapen Barat).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing: the record gives speaker ethnonym, villages, neighbouring languages and a dialectometry percentage; no wordlist and no phonology on the page.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert & Stephen Trussel. Austronesian Comparative Dictionary, CLDF edition (lexibank/acd), languages table.
sources.note: ACD 'Marau_1' (mara1397) has Source = anceaux1961, so its Marau forms carry no stress information; a second row 'Marau_2' (source Tryon & Hackman 1983, Solomon Islands) is mis-mapped to mara1397.
